4.3. In the Reference Petition, under Section 18 of the Act, the award has been challenged, on the ground, of that the learned Collector has not assessed the market value of the acquired land, as per the prevailing rates.
rt According to the petitioners, the learned Collector has assessed the market value of the acquired land at a very low price.

4.4. The petitioners have pleaded that the acquired land is situated in the periphery of the industrial hub and having commercial potentiality, but, this fact has not been considered by the learned Collector.

The market value of the acquired land, prior to the notification, under Section 4 of the Act,
is stated to be more than  25,00,000/- per bigha, whereas, a meagre amount has been paid for the acquired land.
5. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made by the petitioners, before the learned trial Court, to enhance the amount of compensation, as prayed for.

. 
6. When put to notice, the Reference Petition has been contested by the respondents, by taking preliminary objections that the petitioner is hopelessly barred by limitation.

The factum of acquisition of land has not been of disputed, however, the plea, as raised by the petitioners, has been controverted, on the ground, that the learned rt Collector has assessed the market value of the land,
after taking into consideration all the relevant factors.
As such, a prayer has been made to dismiss the Reference Petition.

on the ground that the learned trial Court has gravely erred in law of and facts by awarding flat rate of  6,66,000/- per bigha, irrespective of the classification of land.
